verdict: MARKOV CHAIN FOR 'OUT OF THE GAME'. A plain random walk would have been a rerun -- cascade_all measured RWR inside an XGBoost and the whole G-specific layer hit AUPRC 0.0661 against a 0.0625 base rate, lift 1.06, chance -- so this chain changes six things the data forces: it propagates LOSS OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL DRIVE (1 - fraction remaining, the exact quantity the Replogle matrix stores); it is SEEDED WITH THE MEASURED KNOCKDOWN because these are partial (42.8% of control still present at the median target, only 21% reaching <=5%); it is SIGNED; it is TRUNCATED at K steps and K is swept, because propagating to convergence is the documented failure mode; it aggregates PATH MULTIPLICITY, the one multi-hop effect that survived in multihop_diagnosis; and it is run on two graphs because 91% of the regulatory edges carry no sign at all. THE TARGET IS RARE, WHICH IS ITSELF THE HEADLINE: out-of-the-game (z <= -4.2 AND <= 5% of control left) happens to a MEDIAN OF 0 genes per knockout, mean 1.15, base rate 1.6e-04. A single knockout almost never drives another gene fully out of the game. RESULT on held-out knockouts: chain AUPRC 0.0012 (7.0x lift), one-hop 0.0011, generic-responsiveness null 0.0217 (132x), sign-shuffled 0.0007, seed-shuffled 0.0005; precision@10 0.001 against the null's 0.098. THE CHAIN IS SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE THAN THE GENERIC-RESPONSIVENESS NULL -- paired -0.02059 +- 0.00221, a 9-sigma defeat, with the null scoring 19x the chain. That null -- how often each gene is driven out of the game by ANY knockout, fitted on training knockouts only -- carries far more information than the mechanism, exactly as in cascade_all. WHICH GENES GET SWITCHED OFF IS MOSTLY A PROPERTY OF THE GENE, NOT OF THE KNOCKOUT. Iterating past one step is statistically detectable but negligible (+0.00003 +- 0.00001, +2% of the chain's own score). Edge SIGN carries no detectable information: shuffling signs while holding topology and magnitudes fixed moves the score +0.00049 +- 0.00032. AND THE CHAIN IS NOT DEMONSTRABLY KNOCKOUT-SPECIFIC: seeding it at a RANDOM gene moves the score only +0.00063 +- 0.00057, so it is largely ranking well-connected genes rather than responding to which gene was actually hit. Depth and graph were pre-registered on an inner split of each training fold (chosen: [('signed_only', (6, 0.5)), ('signed_only', (6, 0.5)), ('signed_only', (3, 0.6)), ('signed_only', (6, 0.5)), ('signed_only', (6, 0.5))]), so the headline is not the maximum over a sweep. WHAT THIS CANNOT SAY: 'out of the game' is defined transcriptionally at <= 5% of control mRNA -- not protein loss, not functional failure, and knockdown_dose established this screen cannot locate the level at which a gene stops working. AND THE GRAPH IS PART OF THE PROBLEM: the dense unsigned bulk gives a median out-degree of 329, so one step already touches a large slice of the graph and there is no locality for a path method to exploit; the signed-only graph (54,128 edges, median out-degree 6) scores ~3x better and was pre-registered by every fold, so carrying the unsigned 91% at half weight was actively harmful. Deterministic given seed 0.
